title: Dwelling policies: DP-1, DP-2, DP-3 and their add-ons
summary: The Millers become landlords in Lansing: pick a dwelling form, learn the letters A to E, and patch the gaps with the right add-ons.
objectives: Tell DP-1, DP-2 and DP-3 apart by perils and loss settlement
Match dwelling Coverages A to E, and know liability needs the PLS
Pick Broad or Limited Theft by who lives in the dwelling
Spot the general exclusions and the main dwelling endorsements

scenes.title: The Millers become landlords
scenes.subtitle: Dwelling policies: the 1988 DP-1 and DP-2, the 2002 DP-3, their coverages and their add-ons

beats.text: Sam and Jen Miller just bought a rental house in Lansing. They won't live there. Their tenant, Rosa, moves in Saturday.
beats.say: Sam and Jen Miller just bought a rental house in Lansing. They won't live there. Their tenant, Rosa, moves in Saturday.

beats.text: We're landlords! Now, how do we insure this place?
beats.say: We're landlords! Now, how do we insure this place?

scenes.title: Dana's answer: a dwelling policy
scenes.src: ISO Dwelling Program eligibility (FC&S); DP 00 01 07 88; DP 00 02 07 88; DP 00 03 12 02 (same numbers in 07 14)
scenes.plain: Property insurance for a home for 1 to 4 families, whether or not the owner lives there. It has no liability coverage at all.
scenes.example: The Millers' Lansing rental: they own it, and Rosa lives in it. A two-family duplex could use one too.
scenes.exam: Unlike homeowners forms: no liability or medical payments. Our forms: 1988 DP-1 and DP-2, 2002 DP-3 (its numbers match the 2014 DP-3).

beats.text: You need a dwelling policy.
beats.say: You need a dwelling policy.

beats.text: It insures a home for 1 to 4 families, whether or not the owner lives there.
beats.say: It insures a home for one to four families, whether or not the owner lives there.

beats.text: Unlike homeowners forms, it has no liability coverage at all.
beats.say: Unlike homeowners forms, it has no liability coverage at all.

scenes.title: Dana's question: what if someone gets hurt?
scenes.src: ISO DL 24 01 12 02, Coverages L–M; DP 00 03 12 02 (no liability); HO 00 03 05 11, Sec. II Coverage E; memory aid mn_prop-11

draw.text: What if someone slips and sues?

beats.text: Before you sign: what if a visitor slips on your icy steps and sues?
beats.say: Before you sign: what if a visitor slips on your icy steps and sues?

options.label: Pick the DP-3: the Special Form covers it
options.fail: No dwelling form includes liability or medical payments, not even the DP-3. Add the Personal Liability Supplement.

beats.text: January: a visitor slips and sues. Even the Special Form has no liability coverage, so it pays nothing.
beats.say: January: a visitor slips and sues. Even the Special Form has no liability coverage, so it pays nothing.

options.label: Liability is Coverage E, like our homeowners
options.fail: Dwelling Coverage E is additional living expense, not liability. The letters shift between homeowners and dwelling forms.

beats.text: Nope. In a dwelling policy, E is additional living expense. It pays nothing on a lawsuit.
beats.say: Nope. In a dwelling policy, E is additional living expense. It pays nothing on a lawsuit.

options.label: Add the Personal Liability Supplement
options.win: Dwelling forms have no liability coverage. The Personal Liability Supplement (PLS) adds Coverage L and Coverage M.

beats.text: Smart. The supplement adds Coverage L, personal liability, and Coverage M, medical payments to others.
beats.say: Smart. The supplement adds Coverage L, personal liability, and Coverage M, medical payments to others.

reveal.text: Dwelling forms never include liability. Bolt on the PLS: L for Liability, M for Medical.
reveal.say: Dwelling forms never include liability. Bolt on the P L S: L for Liability, M for Medical.

scenes.title: A landlord's alphabet: Coverages A to E
scenes.src: ISO DP 00 03 12 02, Coverages A–E; DP 00 01 07 88 (no Coverage E); DL 24 01 12 02; memory aid mn_prop-11

spots.label: A: Dwelling
spots.text: Coverage A, Dwelling: the house and the structures attached to it. A for Abode.

spots.label: B: Other Structures
spots.text: Coverage B, Other Structures: structures set apart from the house by clear space, like this detached garage. B for Beside it.

spots.label: C: Personal Property
spots.text: Coverage C, Personal Property: the Millers' own furniture and appliances, while on the Described Location. C for Contents.

spots.label: D: Fair Rental Value
spots.text: Coverage D, Fair Rental Value: the rent lost on the part rented out, when a covered loss makes it unfit to live in. D for Dollars from tenants.

spots.label: E: Additional Living Expense
spots.text: Coverage E, Additional Living Expense: if a covered loss forces you out of the home you live in, your necessary extra living costs, like a hotel. Not in the 1988 DP-1.

spots.label: L and M: not in the form
spots.text: Liability isn't in the alphabet. The Personal Liability Supplement adds Coverage L, personal liability, and M, medical payments to others.

beats.text: What does it cover? Dana draws a landlord's alphabet. Tap each glowing spot.
beats.say: What does it cover? Dana draws a landlord's alphabet. Tap each glowing spot.

reveal.text: A is the Abode, B is Beside it, C is Contents. D is Dollars from tenants. E is Extra living costs.
reveal.say: A is the Abode, B is Beside it, C is Contents. D is Dollars from tenants. E is Extra living costs.

reveal.text: Watch out: in homeowners forms, D is Loss of Use and E is Personal Liability.
reveal.say: Watch out: in homeowners forms, D is Loss of Use and E is Personal Liability.

scenes.title: Basic, Broad, Special: pick a form
scenes.src: ISO DP 00 01 07 88; DP 00 02 07 88; DP 00 03 12 02 (Perils Insured Against; Loss Settlement); confusion pair cp_personal-11

draw.text: Dwelling named perils: a guest list
16 named perils on A, B and C
Buildings, if insured to at least 80%

beats.text: Next, pick a form. Named perils work like a guest list: not on the list, not covered.
beats.say: Next, pick a form. Named perils work like a guest list: not on the list, not covered.

beats.text: DP-1, the Basic Form, has a short list: fire or lightning, and internal explosion. Want windstorm or hail? Pay for Extended Coverage, a bundle of extra perils. Vandalism costs its own premium. Losses are paid at actual cash value.
beats.say: D P one, the Basic Form, has a short list: fire or lightning, and internal explosion. Want windstorm or hail? Pay for Extended Coverage, a bundle of extra perils. Vandalism costs its own premium. Losses are paid at actual cash value.

beats.text: DP-2, the Broad Form, has a long list: 16 named perils, on Coverages A, B and C.
beats.say: D P two, the Broad Form, has a long list: sixteen named perils, on Coverages A, B and C.

beats.text: DP-3, the Special Form, flips it for the buildings: any direct physical loss gets in, unless it's excluded. Contents stay on a named list.
beats.say: D P three, the Special Form, flips it for the buildings: any direct physical loss gets in, unless it's excluded. Contents stay on a named list.

beats.text: DP-2 and DP-3 pay buildings at replacement cost, with nothing off for depreciation, if insured to at least 80% of replacement cost.
beats.say: D P two and D P three pay buildings at replacement cost, with nothing off for depreciation, if insured to at least eighty percent of replacement cost.

scenes.title: DP-1, DP-2 or DP-3?
scenes.src: ISO DP 00 01 07 88; DP 00 02 07 88; DP 00 03 12 02; confusion pair cp_personal-11 (drills)

cards.text: Fire, lightning and internal explosion. Windstorm or hail only for an extra premium.
cards.why: The 1988 DP-1 Basic Form: a short list. Extended Coverage perils and vandalism each need their own premium.

cards.text: The house is covered for any direct physical loss unless the loss is excluded.
cards.why: Only the DP-3 insures the dwelling and other structures on an open-perils basis.

cards.text: The house is covered for 16 named perils, including freezing and weight of ice, snow or sleet.
cards.why: DP-2 Broad: a long named list. DP-1 doesn't list those perils, and DP-3 covers the house on open perils.

cards.text: Every covered loss, even to the house, is paid at actual cash value.
cards.why: The 1988 DP-1 pays ACV. The DP-2 and DP-3 pay buildings at replacement cost if insured to at least 80%.

cards.text: A named list for the house, but replacement cost when it's insured to at least 80%.
cards.why: DP-2: 16 named perils on A, B and C, and buildings at replacement cost when the 80% test is met.

beats.text: Your turn: which form is it?
beats.say: Your turn: which form is it?

reveal.text: The tell: DP-1 is a short named list paid at actual cash value, DP-2 a long named list, DP-3 open perils on the buildings.
reveal.say: The tell: D P one is a short named list paid at actual cash value, D P two a long named list, D P three open perils on the buildings.

scenes.q: The Millers choose the 2002 DP-3. Which coverages does it insure on an open-perils basis?
scenes.why: The DP-3 covers the dwelling (A) and other structures (B) for direct physical loss unless excluded. Personal property (C) gets named perils only.

beats.text: The Millers pick the DP-3. Which coverages get open perils?
beats.say: The Millers pick the D P three. Which coverages get open perils?

reveal.text: A and B only: the buildings. Personal property stays named perils. No DP form covers contents on open perils.
reveal.say: A and B only: the buildings. Personal property stays named perils. No D P form covers contents on open perils.

scenes.title: Fire at the rental: who pays the lost rent?
scenes.src: ISO DP 00 03 12 02, Coverages A, D–E and Other Coverage 5 (same in 07 14); DP 00 02 07 88, Other Coverage 5; prop-gap-01
scenes.ask: Which coverage pays the lost rent?

beats.text: February. A covered fire leaves the rental unfit to live in.
beats.say: February. A covered fire leaves the rental unfit to live in.

beats.text: I can't live here till it's fixed. No rent till then, okay?
beats.say: I can't live here till it's fixed. No rent till then, okay?

beats.text: Which coverage pays the Millers' lost rent?
beats.say: Which coverage pays the Millers' lost rent?

options.label: Coverage E, Additional Living Expense
options.fail: Coverage E pays the insured's own necessary increase in living expenses. The Millers don't live in the rental.

beats.text: Extra living costs? You still sleep at home in Grand Rapids.
beats.say: Extra living costs? You still sleep at home in Grand Rapids.

options.label: Coverage A, along with the repairs
options.fail: Coverage A pays for the dwelling itself. Rent lost while the house is unfit is Coverage D, Fair Rental Value.

beats.text: Coverage A fixes the house. The lost rent? Different letter.
beats.say: Coverage A fixes the house. The lost rent? Different letter.

options.label: Coverage D, Fair Rental Value
options.win: Coverage D pays the fair rental value of the rented part, less any expenses that do not continue while it's unfit.

beats.text: Right. D pays the lost rent, less any expenses that stop while the house is unfit.
beats.say: Right. D pays the lost rent, less any expenses that stop while the house is unfit.

reveal.text: D keeps paying even if repairs run past the policy's expiration. If the Millers lived there, a hotel bill would be Coverage E.
reveal.say: D keeps paying even if repairs run past the policy's expiration. If the Millers lived there, a hotel bill would be Coverage E.

reveal.text: The 2002 DP-3 adds up to 20% of Coverage A for D and E together, as additional insurance. The 1988 DP-2: 10%.
reveal.say: The two thousand two D P three adds up to twenty percent of Coverage A for D and E together, as additional insurance. The nineteen eighty eight D P two: ten percent.

scenes.title: The burglar's dents, not his loot
scenes.src: ISO DP 00 03 12 02, Perils A and Coverage C Perils 8–9; DP 00 02 07 88, Perils 8–9; Dwelling Manual Rule 510; mn_prop-12
scenes.plain: A named personal property peril in the DP-2 and DP-3: damage burglars do to covered property, but not theft.
scenes.example: A burglar pries open the rental's back door and takes the TV the Millers keep there. The crowbar dents: covered. The TV, with no theft endorsement: not covered.
scenes.exam: Homeowners forms list theft. Dwelling forms add it by endorsement, picked by who lives there.

beats.text: In May, with Rosa back, a burglar pries open the back door and grabs the Millers' TV.
beats.say: In May, with Rosa back, a burglar pries open the back door and grabs the Millers' T V.

beats.text: Here's the gap: DP-2 and DP-3 cover damage by burglars, but not theft.
beats.say: Here's the gap: D P two and D P three cover damage by burglars, but not theft.

beats.text: The Millers' policy pays for the burglar's crowbar dents, not his loot.
beats.say: The Millers' policy pays for the burglar's crowbar dents, not his loot.

beats.text: Watch out: homeowners forms list theft. Dwelling forms add it by endorsement.
beats.say: Watch out: homeowners forms list theft. Dwelling forms add it by endorsement.

scenes.title: Which theft endorsement for a landlord?
scenes.src: ISO Dwelling Policy Program Manual Rule 510.A; DP 00 03 12 02, Coverage C perils; question prop-026; memory aid mn_prop-12

beats.text: The Millers want theft coverage for their things in the rental, where they don't live.
beats.say: The Millers want theft coverage for their things in the rental, where they don't live.

beats.text: Theft endorsements go by who lives there. Broad Theft: the named insured lives there, as owner or tenant. Limited Theft: the named insured doesn't.
beats.say: Theft endorsements go by who lives there. Broad Theft: the named insured lives there, as owner or tenant. Limited Theft: the named insured doesn't.

beats.text: Which one fits the Millers?
beats.say: Which one fits the Millers?

options.label: None needed: the DP-3 is open perils
options.fail: The DP-3's open perils cover only the buildings. Its personal property perils include damage by burglars, but not theft.

beats.text: June: a burglar grabs the new TV. Still not covered: DP-3 personal property perils don't include theft.
beats.say: June: a burglar grabs the new T V. Still not covered: D P three personal property perils don't include theft.

options.label: Broad Theft: on and off premises
options.fail: Broad Theft fits an owner-occupant, or a tenant who is the named insured. A landlord who doesn't live there gets Limited Theft.

beats.text: Broad Theft? The named insured has to live there. Rosa does, but the policy is yours.
beats.say: Broad Theft? The named insured has to live there. Rosa does, but the policy is yours.

draw.text: Rosa lives here. The Millers don't.

options.label: Limited Theft: on premises only
options.win: Limited Theft Coverage, on premises only, is for non-owner-occupied risks, like a landlord's rental.

beats.text: Right. Limited Theft covers theft on premises, right where the Millers' things are.
beats.say: Right. Limited Theft covers theft on premises, right where the Millers' things are.

reveal.text: Pick by who lives there, not by price. Rosa lives there, but the named insureds, the Millers, don't.
reveal.say: Pick by who lives there, not by price. Rosa lives there, but the named insureds, the Millers, don't.

reveal.text: Broad Theft can add off-premises coverage, but only with on-premises coverage, at a limit no higher.
reveal.say: Broad Theft can add off-premises coverage, but only with on-premises coverage, at a limit no higher.

scenes.title: Even open-perils coverage has exclusions
scenes.src: ISO DP 00 03 12 02, General Exclusions A.1–9 (same in 07 14); memory hook mn_prop-22
scenes.hook: Old Ernie's Wet Pontoon Never Went North In Grayling.
items: Ordinance or law, Earth movement, Water
Power failure off the location, Neglect, War
Nuclear hazard, Intentional loss, Governmental action
They apply no matter what other cause contributes

beats.text: Even open perils come with exclusions. In the DP-3, nine general ones fit one sentence: Old Ernie's Wet Pontoon Never Went North In Grayling.
beats.say: Even open perils come with exclusions. In the D P three, nine general ones fit one sentence: Old Ernie's Wet Pontoon Never Went North In Grayling.

beats.text: Ordinance or law, earth movement, water. Power failure off the location, neglect, war. Nuclear hazard, intentional loss, governmental action.
beats.say: Ordinance or law, earth movement, water. Power failure off the location, neglect, war. Nuclear hazard, intentional loss, governmental action.

beats.text: They apply no matter what other cause contributes.
beats.say: They apply no matter what other cause contributes.

scenes.title: Excluded cause, covered fire
scenes.src: ISO DP 00 03 12 02, General Exclusions A.2 Earth Movement and A.3 Water Damage (same in 07 14); question prop-gap-05

beats.text: Say an earthquake cracks the rental's foundation. Excluded: earth movement.
beats.say: Say an earthquake cracks the rental's foundation. Excluded: earth movement.

beats.text: But if it breaks a gas line and fire follows, the fire damage is covered.
beats.say: But if it breaks a gas line and fire follows, the fire damage is covered.

beats.text: Water works the same way: flood, sewer or drain backup, and subsurface water are excluded, but an ensuing fire or explosion is covered.
beats.say: Water works the same way: flood, sewer or drain backup, and subsurface water are excluded, but an ensuing fire or explosion is covered.

scenes.title: Under the DP-3: covered or excluded?
scenes.src: ISO DP 00 03 12 02, Perils A–B and General Exclusions A.2–A.3 (same in 07 14); questions prop-gap-05, prop-gap-06

items.why: Earth movement is excluded, whatever else contributes.

items.text: Fire from the gas line the quake broke
items.why: Fire or explosion that results from earth movement is covered.

items.text: The Grand River floods the basement
items.why: Flood is part of the water damage exclusion.

items.text: Sewage backs up through a floor drain
items.why: Water that backs up through sewers or drains is excluded.

items.text: Wind tears shingles off the roof
items.why: Not a general exclusion, and the DP-3 covers the house for direct physical loss unless excluded.

items.text: A tree limb falls on the roof
items.why: Not a general exclusion: covered under the DP-3's open perils on the dwelling.

beats.text: Your turn: covered, or excluded?
beats.say: Your turn: covered, or excluded?

reveal.text: Earth movement and water are excluded, whatever else contributes. But a fire or explosion they cause is covered.
reveal.say: Earth movement and water are excluded, whatever else contributes. But a fire or explosion they cause is covered.

reveal.text: Wind and a falling limb aren't excluded, so the DP-3 covers them.
reveal.say: Wind and a falling limb aren't excluded, so the D P three covers them.

scenes.title: Three more endorsements to know
scenes.src: ISO DP 04 11 12 02; DP 11 43 12 02; FC&S (Aug. 12, 2024) on Special Provisions DP 01 XX (Michigan: DP 01 21)

draw.text: A and B limits rise yearly by the % shown, pro rata
Worth half its finished value? Half the limit.
State-mandated changes, notably cancellation and nonrenewal

beats.text: Three more endorsements. Automatic Increase in Insurance raises the Coverage A and B limits each year by the percentage shown, applied pro rata over the policy period.
beats.say: Three more endorsements. Automatic Increase in Insurance raises the Coverage A and B limits each year by the percentage shown, applied pro rata over the policy period.

beats.text: Building a house? Dwelling Under Construction makes the Coverage A limit provisional. On any date, the insurance is that limit times actual value over completed value. Worth half its finished value? Half the limit.
beats.say: Building a house? Dwelling Under Construction makes the Coverage A limit provisional. On any date, the insurance is that limit times actual value over completed value. Worth half its finished value? Half the limit.

beats.text: And Michigan's own endorsement, Special Provisions – Michigan, makes the state-mandated changes, notably to cancellation and nonrenewal.
beats.say: And Michigan's own endorsement, Special Provisions, Michigan, makes the state mandated changes, notably to cancellation and nonrenewal.

items: DP-1: short named list, ACV. DP-2: 16 named perils. DP-3: open A and B
Dwelling D is fair rental value; E is additional living expense
No liability in DP forms: add the PLS for Coverages L and M
Theft by endorsement: Broad if named insured lives there, else Limited
Earth movement and water excluded; ensuing fire is covered

beats.text: What a year! DP-1 has a short list and pays actual cash value. DP-2 has a long list. DP-3 covers the buildings on open perils.
beats.say: What a year! D P one has a short list and pays actual cash value. D P two has a long list. D P three covers the buildings on open perils.

beats.text: D pays lost rent, and E your own extra living costs. Liability needs the PLS, and theft an endorsement picked by who lives there.
beats.say: D pays lost rent, and E your own extra living costs. Liability needs the P L S, and theft an endorsement picked by who lives there.

beats.text: And a fire that follows an earthquake or flood is covered.
beats.say: And a fire that follows an earthquake or flood is covered.

beats.text: Landlording: harder than it looks!
beats.say: Landlording: harder than it looks!
